transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m making a big deal out of nothing, but I’m not. My family and my friends keep pointing at these bank papers like, “See, nothing was taken,” but papers can be made to look a certain way, you know? And this has been going on for over a year.

They’re hiding my money. I know they are. They use bills and fundraisers and all these trip plans—like suddenly there’s always some reason money is moving around—and then when I ask, they act like I’m the problem. My cousin did that same thing with a church raffle once, not exactly the same, but people think if it’s written down then it’s true.

So I came because they keep telling me to talk to someone, but really I need somebody to understand why I have to keep confronting them. They need to tell the truth.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

I don’t… I mean, I don’t think so. Not like somebody standing there talking when no one’s there. Sometimes I’ll be alone and I’ll hear the TV from next door or people outside, and then it makes me think about what they’re saying or what they’re planning, because people do talk, you know? Like my aunt used to whisper in the kitchen and then say she wasn’t saying anything. But voices, like just out of nowhere? I haven’t really noticed that.
Do people ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or that your thoughts seem jumbled?

I don’t know… people say I talk “too much” or I don’t get to the point, but that’s because there’s a lot of parts to it. Like if I’m explaining one thing, I have to explain what happened before, otherwise they’ll twist it and say I never said that. My sister does that, she’ll act like she doesn’t remember, and then suddenly everyone is looking at me like I’m the confusing one.

So… hard to follow? Maybe they say that, but I don’t think my thoughts are jumbled. I think they just don’t want to listen all the way.
Before this money issue started, did you generally have a hard time trusting people?

I don’t know… I mean, what do you mean by “hard time”? I always noticed when people were acting funny, if that’s what you mean. But everybody notices stuff, right? Like if someone says they’ll call and then they don’t, or they smile one way in front of you and another way when someone else walks in.

Before all this, I guess I just kept my eyes open. My grandma used to say you don’t tell everybody your business, because people use it. And she wasn’t wrong—there was this lady at the corner store who would repeat everything she heard, even about people’s kids, and then act innocent. So trusting people… I don’t know. I trusted some people. Not everybody. You can’t trust everybody.
Before the money problem began, did you often think people were trying to take advantage of you?

I don’t know if I’d say “often.” I mean, people try to get over on people all the time, that’s just how it is. Like at stores, they’ll ring something up wrong and then act like you’re bothering them when you ask. And my cousin used to borrow little things and not bring them back, but everybody acted like that was normal because she was “family.”

Before the money thing… I guess I noticed when somebody wasn’t being straight. But taking advantage, like everybody was out to do that? I don’t know. I wasn’t walking around thinking that all day. I just didn’t like being played, that’s all.
Do you think there is anything impossible or beyond ordinary methods about how they are hiding your money?

I don’t mean like magic or something, if that’s what you’re asking. It’s ordinary ways, but sneaky ways. Like they keep showing me these bank papers and saying, “See, nothing was taken,” but papers can be moved around, bills can be made to look one way, and then there’s fundraisers and trip plans mixed in so nobody can tell what went where.

That’s why I keep asking them, because it’s been over a year and I know they’re hiding my money. They want me to stop bringing it up, but if I stop, then they just get away with it. My family and even friends keep acting like I’m not seeing it right, but they’re covering it up. They need to just tell the truth.
Have you ever felt like someone could put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of it?

Put thoughts in? I don’t… I don’t think so. Like, people can get in your head by talking too much, you know? My aunt does that, she’ll keep saying the same thing until you start hearing it even when she’s not there, but that’s not like taking thoughts out.

I’ve had people try to confuse me, definitely. They say things one way and then later say they never said it, and then you start questioning yourself. But someone actually putting a thought in my mind or removing one… I don’t know. I haven’t noticed that kind of thing.
Is it possible you could be mistaken about your family hiding your money?

Mistaken? I mean… people keep saying that, that I’m “mistaken,” because they wave the bank papers around like that proves everything. But papers don’t show everything. Bills get moved around, fundraisers, trips, all that stuff gets mixed together, and then nobody can tell where the money really went.

And my family keeps acting like I’m the problem for asking. My friends too, they say to leave it alone, but it’s been over a year. I know they’re hiding it. I didn’t come here because I’m confused about that, I came because everybody keeps trying to make me stop talking about it. If they would just tell the truth, I wouldn’t have to keep confronting them.
Aside from this issue with your money, have you been able to work and handle your usual day-to-day responsibilities normally?

Yeah, I mean, mostly. I don’t have a job right now, but I still do my regular things. I make my own food, I get myself to the county clinic and those assistance appointments, and I keep my stuff in order.

It’s really just when the money thing comes up, then there’s arguing, because they act like I’m supposed to just forget it. But day to day, I’m not helpless or anything. I do what I have to do.
Have people told you that you seem emotionally flat or don’t show much feeling?

Emotionally flat? I don’t know… people say all kinds of things when they want you to stop talking. My cousin will say I’m “cold” if I don’t react the way she wants, but then if I do get upset, she says I’m making a scene, so what am I supposed to do with that?

I mean, I laugh at things. I get mad, I get worried. Maybe I don’t always show it on my face right away. Sometimes I’m just thinking, and people think that means something. I don’t know if that’s the same as flat. What do you mean by that exactly?
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic or high, like you needed much less sleep than usual?

Unusually energetic… I don’t know. I have nights where I don’t sleep good, but that’s not like I’m “high” or whatever. Sometimes I’m just thinking too much, and then the next day I’m tired and people still expect me to go stand in lines at those offices, and the buses don’t even run right half the time.

So… less sleep, maybe sometimes, but not because I’m feeling great or anything. I don’t think I get that way. What do you mean by unusually energetic?
Other than the money issue, do you believe anyone is trying to harm, cheat, or spy on you?

I mean… not spy like cameras or anything, if that’s what you mean. But cheat, yeah, that’s kind of the whole thing. My family and some people I thought were friends keep acting like the bank papers prove nothing happened, but they don’t. They’re hiding where the money went.

It’s been over a year, and every time I bring it up there’s some new excuse—bills, or some fundraiser, or somebody planning a trip like that’s supposed to explain everything. And then they say I’m the problem because I keep asking. But if someone was taking from you and covering it up, you wouldn’t just sit there either. So I keep confronting them because somebody needs to finally tell the truth.
Before the money problem started, did you often believe people were deliberately plotting against you?

Before? I mean, people have always had their little ways, you know, saying one thing and doing another, but this isn’t me just thinking everybody’s plotting. I came in because of the money.

My family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but those papers don’t explain everything. For over a year I’ve known they’re hiding where my money went, and then they bring up bills or fundraisers or somebody’s trip like that covers it up. So I have to keep asking them, confronting them, because nobody wants to tell the truth.
Have you ever felt that outside forces were controlling your actions?

Outside forces? I don’t know what that means exactly. Like somebody making my arms move or making me do things? No… I don’t think so.

Sometimes people push you, though, like they keep talking and talking until you have to go deal with something, and then everybody acts like you’re the one causing trouble. My aunt used to do that too, just keep pressing until you answer, but that’s not like… controlling my body or anything. I make my own choices, far as I know.
Before the money problem began, did you usually keep your distance from people because you felt they might use you or betray you?

I don’t know… I mean, I wasn’t sitting around thinking everybody was gonna betray me all the time, if that’s what you mean. I’ve always been careful with people, because people talk and then they twist things, and my cousin used to do that with everybody’s business, not just mine.

But keeping distance? I don’t really know. Sometimes I just didn’t feel like being around people, and then other times I’d be around them if there was food or something going on. It wasn’t like I had some rule about it. The money thing is different. That’s when it became clear something wasn’t right.
Did this belief that your family was hiding your money come on suddenly?

Not like overnight, no. It was more when my income dropped… about a year and two months ago, that’s when I started seeing how things weren’t adding up.

At first I was just trying to stretch what I had, you know, and then you notice little things—well, not little, but people act like you’re being dramatic. And my sister, she’ll talk about prices going up like that explains everything, but it doesn’t. So… it’s been going on since around then.
Do you ever feel that things like TV shows, radio, or people talking nearby are sending messages meant specifically for you?

TV shows? No, I don’t really watch like that… I mean sometimes the TV’s on in the background, and people on there talk crazy anyway, like those court shows where everybody’s yelling. My neighbor used to have one playing loud through the wall, and you can hear bits of it, but that’s just noise.

People talking nearby, I notice if they get quiet when I come around, but messages like… meant for me from the radio or something? I don’t think so. I wouldn’t say that.
Before the money problem started, did you tend to hold grudges for a long time when you felt people had wronged or insulted you?

I don’t know… grudges sounds like such a strong word. If somebody does something wrong, I remember it, because you’re not supposed to just let people keep doing things to you. But before all this money stuff, I wasn’t like sitting there making a list or nothing.

Like, people in my family say things and then act like they didn’t, and that gets under my skin. My aunt used to do that at cookouts, she’d make little comments and then laugh, and everybody would just keep eating like it was normal. So I guess I’d stay annoyed for a while, but I don’t know if that’s a grudge. Depends what they did.
Before the money problem started, did you often feel that ordinary comments from people were really meant as hidden insults or threats toward you?

I don’t know about threats. Hidden insults… maybe sometimes people say things in a way, like they’ll smile but it don’t feel friendly. But before the money thing, I wasn’t thinking every little comment was some secret code or nothing.

People do make remarks, though. Like my cousin used to say, “Some people need to learn how to manage,” and everybody would laugh, and I’m like, why say that right when I walk in? But then she says she meant the TV, or somebody else, and then it turns into me being too sensitive. That kind of stuff sticks with you.

So… often? I don’t know. I noticed when people were being slick, but I wouldn’t say I was walking around scared of comments or thinking they were threats.
Before the money problem started, did you usually suspect that people were lying to you even when you didn’t have clear proof?

I mean… lying? I don’t know. People lie sometimes, everybody knows that. Like if somebody says they called and they didn’t, or they say they’re “on the way” and they still in the house, that’s just people being people.

Before the money thing, I wasn’t just going around saying everybody was lying to me. I might wonder if something sounded funny, but clear proof… I don’t know. Sometimes you can tell by somebody’s face, though, the way they look away or start talking too much. My sister does that when she don’t want to answer straight, and then she gets mad if you ask again.

But usually? I’m not sure. I paid attention, I guess. I wouldn’t say I suspected everybody all the time.

It wasn’t like I had some rule about it. The money thing is different. That’s when it became clear something wasn’t right.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was an acute onset of the persecutory belief, which best distinguishes persistent delusional disorder from schizophrenia, acute polymorphic psychotic disorder, and paranoid personality disorder.
doctor.question: Did this belief that your family was hiding your money come on suddenly?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on since my income dropped, about a year and two months ago.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about when and how the belief began, which is most directly related to the symptom duration/onset information.

patient.answer:
Not like overnight, no. It was more when my income dropped… about a year and two months ago, that’s when I started seeing how things weren’t adding up.

At first I was just trying to stretch what I had, you know, and then you notice little things—well, not little, but people act like you’re being dramatic. And my sister, she’ll talk about prices going up like that explains everything, but it doesn’t. So… it’s been going on since around then.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the persecutory belief is accompanied by broader schizophrenic-spectrum symptoms by testing for ideas of reference, helping distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum or acute psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Do you ever feel that things like TV shows, radio, or people talking nearby are sending messages meant specifically for you?

target_item.reason: The question is about whether TV, radio, or nearby conversations send special messages meant for me, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile focused on the fixed belief about family hiding money.

patient.answer:
TV shows? No, I don’t really watch like that… I mean sometimes the TV’s on in the background, and people on there talk crazy anyway, like those court shows where everybody’s yelling. My neighbor used to have one playing loud through the wall, and you can hear bits of it, but that’s just noise.

People talking nearby, I notice if they get quiet when I come around, but messages like… meant for me from the radio or something? I don’t think so. I wouldn’t say that.

inference.note: F23.3 ruled out: belief has persisted >1 year with gradual onset rather than acute/transient psychosis. Presentation most supports a single non-bizarre persecutory delusion with otherwise preserved functioning and no clear hallucinations, thought insertion, passivity, negative symptoms, or prominent disorganization. F20.0 remains less likely but not fully excluded; F60.0 remains a personality-level alternative given longstanding guardedness, though pre-morbid pervasive paranoia is not well established.

doctor.intent: Differentiate a fixed circumscribed delusion from a longstanding pervasive suspicious personality style by assessing whether she held a grudge over perceived insults for a long time before the money issue.
doctor.question: Before the money problem started, did you tend to hold grudges for a long time when you felt people had wronged or insulted you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a long-standing personality pattern before the money problem, specifically whether the patient tended to hold grudges; the provided symptom profiles only cover the current delusion, duration, and functioning/impairment, not premorbid grudges or personality traits.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… grudges sounds like such a strong word. If somebody does something wrong, I remember it, because you’re not supposed to just let people keep doing things to you. But before all this money stuff, I wasn’t like sitting there making a list or nothing.

Like, people in my family say things and then act like they didn’t, and that gets under my skin. My aunt used to do that at cookouts, she’d make little comments and then laugh, and everybody would just keep eating like it was normal. So I guess I’d stay annoyed for a while, but I don’t know if that’s a grudge. Depends what they did.

doctor.intent: Distinguish a circumscribed persistent delusion from a longstanding paranoid personality pattern by testing for excessive suspicious interpretation of benign remarks before the money issue began.
doctor.question: Before the money problem started, did you often feel that ordinary comments from people were really meant as hidden insults or threats toward you?

target_item.reason: The question asks about longstanding suspicious interpretation of ordinary comments as hidden insults or threats before the money delusion began, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know about threats. Hidden insults… maybe sometimes people say things in a way, like they’ll smile but it don’t feel friendly. But before the money thing, I wasn’t thinking every little comment was some secret code or nothing.

People do make remarks, though. Like my cousin used to say, “Some people need to learn how to manage,” and everybody would laugh, and I’m like, why say that right when I walk in? But then she says she meant the TV, or somebody else, and then it turns into me being too sensitive. That kind of stuff sticks with you.

So… often? I don’t know. I noticed when people were being slick, but I wouldn’t say I was walking around scared of comments or thinking they were threats.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the suspiciousness and mistrust were a longstanding personality pattern before the fixed money belief, which would help distinguish paranoid personality disorder from delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Before the money problem started, did you usually suspect that people were lying to you even when you didn’t have clear proof?

target_item.reason: The question asks about suspiciousness before the money problem started, specifically whether I generally suspected people were lying without proof. The provided symptom profile covers the current delusion about money, duration, and functioning, but not premorbid suspiciousness or paranoid personality traits.

patient.answer:
I mean… lying? I don’t know. People lie sometimes, everybody knows that. Like if somebody says they called and they didn’t, or they say they’re “on the way” and they still in the house, that’s just people being people.

Before the money thing, I wasn’t just going around saying everybody was lying to me. I might wonder if something sounded funny, but clear proof… I don’t know. Sometimes you can tell by somebody’s face, though, the way they look away or start talking too much. My sister does that when she don’t want to answer straight, and then she gets mad if you ask again.

But usually? I’m not sure. I paid attention, I guess. I wouldn’t say I suspected everybody all the time.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusion focused on family/friends hiding their money for over one year, with preserved overall functioning and no clear hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal, control phenomena, prominent disorganization, negative symptoms, or mood episode syndrome. This supports delusional disorder rather than schizophrenia or paranoid personality disorder.
